wacky.example: some wacky plan for selling more books

wagon.meaning: any of various kinds of wheeled vehicles drawn by an animal or a tractor

waist.meaning: the narrowing of the body between the ribs and hips

waltz.meaning: a graceful ballroom dance in three-time

warty.meaning: (of skin) covered with warts or projections that resemble warts

waste.example: He wasted his inheritance on his insincere friends

watch.meaning: look at attentively; a small clock worn on the wrist

water.meaning: the clear liquid that falls as rain and fills rivers and seas

waver.meaning: pause or hold back in uncertainty or unwillingness

waxen.meaning: made of or covered with wax

weave.meaning: interlace by or as if by weaving

wedge.meaning: a piece thick at one end and thin at the other

whale.meaning: a huge sea mammal that breathes through a blowhole

wharf.meaning: a platform built out from the shore into the water and supported by piles

wheat.meaning: the grain ground into flour for bread and roti

wheel.meaning: a simple machine consisting of a circular frame with spokes (or a solid disc) that can rotate on a shaft or axle (as…

whelp.meaning: young of any of various canines such as a dog or wolf

which.meaning: asking or specifying one out of a set

while.meaning: a period of indeterminate length (usually short) marked by some action or condition
while.example: he was here for a little while

whine.meaning: complain in an annoying voice; a high-pitched cry

whirl.meaning: turn in a twisting or spinning motion

whisk.meaning: beat eggs or cream quickly; the tool for it

white.meaning: being of the achromatic color of maximum lightness

whoop.meaning: shout, as if with joy or enthusiasm
whoop.example: The children whooped when they were led to the picnic table

widen.meaning: become broader or wider or more extensive

widow.meaning: a woman whose husband is dead especially one who has not remarried

width.meaning: the extent of something from side to side

wince.meaning: draw back, as with fear or pain

winch.meaning: lifting device consisting of a horizontal cylinder turned by a crank on which a cable or rope winds

windy.meaning: abounding in or exposed to the wind or breezes

witty.meaning: combining clever conception and facetious expression
witty.example: his sermons were unpredictably witty and satirical as well as eloquent

woman.meaning: an adult female person (as opposed to a man)
woman.example: the woman kept house while the man hunted

woody.meaning: made of or containing or resembling wood

wooer.meaning: a man who courts a woman

woozy.meaning: having or causing a whirling sensation
woozy.example: feeling woozy from the blow on his head

wordy.meaning: using or containing too many words
wordy.example: newspapers of the day printed long wordy editorials

worry.meaning: be worried, concerned, anxious, troubled, or uneasy

worse.meaning: (comparative of `bad') inferior to another in quality or condition or desirability
worse.example: this road is worse than the first one we took

worst.meaning: (superlative of `bad') most wanting in quality or value or condition
worst.example: the worst player on the team

worth.meaning: (often used ironically) worthy of being treated in a particular way

would.meaning: past of will: used for imagined situations, wishes and polite requests

wound.meaning: an injury to living tissue (especially an injury involving a cut or break in the skin)

woven.meaning: made or constructed by interlacing threads or strips of material or other elements into a whole

wrack.meaning: destruction, in 'wrack and ruin'; also seaweed

wrath.meaning: intense anger (usually on an epic scale)

wreak.meaning: cause to happen or to occur as a consequence

wrest.meaning: obtain by seizing forcibly or violently, also metaphorically
wrest.example: wrest the knife from his hands

wring.meaning: twist and squeeze to force out liquid

wrist.meaning: a joint between the distal end of the radius and the proximal row of carpal bones

wrong.example: the report in the paper is wrong

wrote.meaning: past tense of write: put words on paper or a screen
